title: Neapolitan-style pizza Margherita

ingredients.note: canned whole peeled San Marzano style, crushed by hand
fior di latte, torn and drained

steps: Dissolve the salt in the water, then add the yeast. Add the flour and mix until combined, then knead for about 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and rest 2 hours at room temperature, then divide into 4 balls and refrigerate in a covered container for 18 to 24 hours.
Take the dough out 1 to 2 hours before baking. Heat the oven with a pizza stone or steel as hot as it will go, at least 250 C, for 45 minutes.
Stretch each ball by hand from the centre outward, leaving a thicker rim. Do not use a rolling pin.
Spread a few spoonfuls of crushed tomato over the base, then add torn mozzarella and a pinch of salt.
Bake for 6 to 8 minutes until the crust is puffed and charred in places and the cheese has melted.
Finish with basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil.
notes: A home oven cannot match a 450 C wood-fired oven, so expect a slightly less charred crust.

title: Tagliatelle with Bolognese-style ragù
steps: Melt the butter in a heavy pot and cook the pancetta until the fat runs. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook gently for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and pork and break them up. Cook, stirring, until the meat is no longer pink and has begun to brown.
Stir in the tomato paste, then pour in the wine and let it bubble until almost gone.
Add the milk and cook until absorbed, then add about 300 ml hot water. Cover partly and simmer on the lowest heat for 2.5 to 3 hours, adding water if it dries out. Season with salt.
For the pasta, pile the flour on a board, make a well, crack in the eggs and work them into a dough. Knead 10 minutes, rest 30 minutes, roll thin and cut into ribbons about 6 mm wide.
Cook the tagliatelle in salted boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes. Toss with the ragù and a little pasta water, and serve with Parmesan.
notes: Dried egg tagliatelle can be used when short of time. Cook according to the package.

title: Sicilian arancini with ragù and peas

ingredients.note: beaten with a splash of water

steps: Cook the rice in the hot stock with the saffron, stirring, for about 18 minutes until tender and sticky. Stir in the butter and Parmesan, spread on a tray and chill completely.
For the filling, fry the onion in a little oil, add the beef and brown it, then add the passata and peas and simmer 15 minutes until thick. Cool.
Wet your hands and take a golf-ball-sized handful of rice. Make a hollow, add a spoonful of ragù and a cube of mozzarella, then close the rice around it and shape into a ball or cone.
Roll each ball in flour, dip in egg, then coat in breadcrumbs. Chill for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil to 170 C and fry the arancini in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden. Drain on paper and serve hot.
notes: Cold rice holds its shape. Day-old risotto works well.

title: Risotto alla milanese

ingredients.note: beef or chicken stock, kept hot
threads, soaked in a ladle of hot stock

steps: Melt half the butter over a low heat and soften the onion without browning, about 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains are glossy and hot.
Pour in the wine and cook until it has evaporated.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring often and waiting for each addition to be absorbed. After about 10 minutes, add the saffron and its stock.
Keep going for another 8 minutes or so until the rice is creamy but still has a slight bite.
Take off the heat, beat in the remaining butter and the Parmesan, cover, and rest for 2 minutes. The risotto should be loose and wavy, not stiff.

title: Carnevale chiacchiere
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, salt and lemon zest. Add the eggs, butter and wine and knead into a firm, smooth dough.
Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out very thin, 1 to 2 mm, in batches. Cut into rectangles or ribbons with a fluted wheel and make a slit in the middle if you like.
Heat the oil to 170 C and fry a few pieces at a time for about 1 minute per side until pale gold and blistered.
Drain on paper and dust generously with icing sugar when cool.
notes: The thinner the dough, the crisper the result. Store in a tin for up to a few days.

title: Tuscan ribollita

ingredients.note: cavolo nero or other dark kale, stems removed, leaves shredded
stale country bread, torn into pieces

steps: Cover the soaked beans with fresh water and simmer for about 1 hour until tender. Do not salt until the end. Keep the cooking water, then lift out about a third of the beans and mash them.
In a large pot, warm 4 tablespoons of the oil and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for a minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, then add the kale, the whole beans, the mashed beans and the bean cooking water topped up with water to about 2 litres.
Simmer gently for 40 minutes until the vegetables are very soft. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the torn bread and cook 10 minutes until it falls apart into a thick soup. Rest the soup for at least a few hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Reheat gently, loosening with a little hot water if needed, and serve each bowl with a thread of raw olive oil.
notes: It tastes better the next day, which is the point of the dish. Cooked canned beans (2 x 400 g tins) can replace the dried ones to save time.

title: Spaghetti alla carbonara
steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil and salt it lightly, as the guanciale and cheese are salty.
Cook the guanciale in a large cold pan over medium-low heat for about 8 minutes until the fat has rendered and the meat is golden and crisp. Turn off the heat.
Whisk the eggs with the pecorino and most of the pepper to a thick paste.
Boil the spaghetti until just al dente. Scoop out a mugful of the cooking water, then drain the pasta.
Add the pasta to the pan with the guanciale and toss. Let it cool for a minute, so that the pan is warm but not sizzling.
Pour in the egg and cheese mixture and toss vigorously, adding a few spoonfuls of the pasta water until you have a glossy cream that coats each strand. Serve at once with the rest of the pepper.
notes: If the pan is too hot the eggs will scramble. Pancetta can replace guanciale, though the flavour is less rounded.

title: Orecchiette with cime di rapa and anchovy

ingredients.note: turnip tops or broccoli rabe, tough stems trimmed

steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Add the greens and cook for 4 minutes, then add the orecchiette to the same water.

While they cook, warm the olive oil in a wide pan over low heat with the garlic, chilli and anchovy fillets. Stir until the anchovies dissolve into the oil, about 3 minutes, without letting the garlic brown.
When the pasta is al dente (usually 11 to 13 minutes in total), lift the pasta and greens out with a spider and add them to the pan along with a ladle of the cooking water.
Toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, crushing some of the greens with a spoon so they coat the pasta. Taste for salt and serve.
notes: Fresh orecchiette cook in about 4 minutes, so add them to the water after the greens have had 8 minutes.

title: Home-baked panettone
steps: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast and salt. Add the lukewarm milk, eggs, vanilla and zest and knead for 10 minutes by machine or 15 by hand until a smooth, sticky dough forms.
Add the softened butter a piece at a time, kneading until fully absorbed and the dough is glossy and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for about 2 hours until doubled.
Knead in the raisins and candied peel. Divide between two 750 g paper panettone moulds, each filled about half way.
Let rise again for 1.5 to 2 hours until the dough reaches about 2 cm below the rim.
Heat the oven to 175 C. Cut a cross on top of each if you like. Bake 45 to 50 minutes until deep golden and a skewer comes out clean, covering with foil after 25 minutes if it browns too fast.
Cool in the moulds on a rack before cutting.
notes: Traditional panettone uses a sourdough starter and takes two days; this yeast version is simpler and still soft. Keeps well wrapped for 4 to 5 days.

title: Home-baked pandoro

ingredients.note: soft, plus extra for the tin

steps: Mix the flour, sugar, yeast, salt, milk, eggs, vanilla and lemon zest and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Knead in the butter a little at a time until the dough is silky and pulls away from the bowl. Cover and let rise for about 2 hours until doubled.
Butter a 1.5 litre star-shaped pandoro mould or deep fluted tin. Shape the dough into a smooth ball, drop it in with the seam down, and cover.
Let it rise for 1.5 to 2 hours until the dough comes close to the rim.
Heat the oven to 170 C. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean, covering with foil if the top browns too quickly.
Cool for 15 minutes, then turn out. Dust thickly with icing sugar before serving.
notes: Bakers add the butter and sugar in stages for a very light crumb; this simplified method keeps the same flavour with less work.
